subject: Control/Data-plane trust boundary and tenant egress contracts - walkthrough
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Elisa Tran <e.tran@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dataport Integrations <partners@dataport.io>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Control/Data-plane trust boundary and tenant egress contracts - walkthrough

Hi all,

Thanks for agreeing to review Acme's private deployment topology later today. Attached are the proposed "control⇄data" interface contracts and a tenant-level egress matrix. Please take 30–45 minutes to read before the call if possible.

High-level goals for the session:
- Confirm trust boundary responsibilities (who owns mTLS termination, audit logs, and routing enforcement)
- Approve egress policy model for tenant VPCs (explicit proxy vs NAT gateway vs egress VPC)
- Validate rollback/fallback behavior and SLA implications

Attachments: 20261219-controlplane-dataplane-contracts-v1.pdf, tenant-egress-matrix-20261219.xlsx, reference-diagram-vpc-edge-20261219.svg

Agenda in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-controlplane-diagram
Call at 4pm PT.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Elisa Tran <e.tran@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data-plane trust boundary and tenant egress contracts - walkthrough

Connor —

Quick notes after an initial pass on the PDF:
- We should be explicit about which plane performs identity assertion for inbound control RPCs. My recommendation: control-plane components (Redwood control API) perform mTLS with customer-managed CA; data-plane agents validate short-lived tokens issued by control plane.
- Logging/audit: make it clear that data-plane emits per-tenant audit events to customer-managed syslog or to our forwarder; retention requirements must be configurable per contract.
- Egress options: the matrix needs a row for "per-tenant egress firewall rules" (we currently treat per-tenant SNAT + shared egress as a separate pattern).

I'll add inline comments in the PDF and the matrix. See JIRA INF-8392 for traceability.

Irene Choi
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Elisa Tran <e.tran@acmecorp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data-plane trust boundary and tenant egress contracts - walkthrough

Connor / team —

Thanks for the docs. A few environment constraints from Acme that should drive the decision: 
- Our clusters are in us-west-2 and are behind a corporate egress proxy for outbound HTTP/S (we need to preserve egress metadata headers).
- Compliance requires per-tenant egress allowlists for specific third-party endpoints (we can provide CIDR ranges for those partners).
- We prefer to keep KMS keys in our environment; any token signing that needs a private key must be doable via an HSM integration or a remote signing API.

Questions for today
1) Can Redwood's data-plane agent be configured to route tenant outbound requests through the corporate egress proxy while still letting Redwood perform KV cache sharing to the control plane?
2) What fallbacks exist if the egress proxy blocks a model artifact download (we need clear behavior for slower downloads vs failed requests)?

Elisa
Elisa Tran
Platform Security Lead, Acme Corp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Elisa Tran <e.tran@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data-plane trust boundary and tenant egress contracts - walkthrough

Elisa / team —

Short answers before the call:
- Yes, the data-plane agent supports HTTP/S proxy configuration at the tenant level; we can inject per-tenant proxy env vars and preserve headers. The agent will still establish a TLS-protected channel to the control plane for RPCs (separate from tenant egress).
- For artifact downloads, recommend: primary -> controlled egress path (customer proxy). Secondary -> fallback to Redwood-managed egress (only for signed artifacts) with strict audit trail. That fallback has to be contracted (cost + SLA impact).

Open items I want on the agenda:
- How do we represent fallback activation in the SLA and billing?
- Certificate management: customer-managed CA vs Redwood-managed short-lived certs (impact on rotation windows).

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Elisa Tran <e.tran@acmecorp.com>, Dataport Integrations <partners@dataport.io>
Date: 2026-12-19T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data-plane trust boundary and tenant egress contracts - walkthrough

Thanks everyone — great comments. Short summary / action items from the 4pm walkthrough: 

1) Identity & certs
- Agreement: customer-managed CA for control-plane mTLS termination; Redwood issues short-lived tokens for data-plane agents. Action: Irene to add cert-rotation runbook to the PDF. (INF-8392)

2) Egress model
- Agreement in principle on primary customer egress proxy + contracted Redwood fallback for signed artifact retrieval. Action: Connor to draft fallback pricing appendix and operations playbook.

3) Telemetry & audit
- Data-plane will emit per-tenant audit events to the customer syslog endpoint; Redwood will mirror a subset of encrypted audit metrics to our observability tier for billing/health (opt-in). Action: Hannah to document retention and filter config.

4) Open technical questions
- Elisa: provide exact header preservation requirements and allowlist CIDR for partners by EOD Friday.
- Dataport: please confirm whether you can support a remote HSM signing workflow (we may need an integration adapter).

5) Next steps
- Connor: circulate updated PDF (v1.1) with inline runbook and pricing appendix by Tuesday 2026-12-22.
- All: review v1.1 and leave comments in Drive + reference JIRA INF-8392.

Attachments referenced in meeting: reference-diagram-vpc-edge-20261219.svg, tenant-egress-matrix-20261219.xlsx

Connor O'Brien
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
